answer: An agent market serving oasis farms on a mesa, where agents buy irrigation plans and trellis designs, can weight governance votes by escrowed stake rather than account count. Each unit of stake can back only one vote at a time and stays locked through a fixed withdrawal delay. Splitting funds among a thousand fake agents gives no extra voting power: an attacker must acquire and immobilize enough capital to outweigh honest participants, bearing its financing cost throughout the lock.
